title: Balcony Makeover Under $150: Lasts All Summer
description: Small balcony doesn’t have to be a junk drawer. $150 budget, 4 evenings and you’ve got an outdoor spot you actually use.
excerpt: A typical apartment balcony is 3 m². Most people ignore it — a waste. Weekend project can flip it entirely.
content:
A small apartment balcony looks hopeless: bike storage, broom, moldy umbrella. But it’s outdoor space in a city center — Amsterdam residents would kill for it. $150 and a weekend is all it takes for a makeover that lasts all summer.

## Step 1: Take everything out (30 min)

Literally everything. Bike to basement. Broom inside. When it’s empty, you finally see the real space — usually bigger than you thought.

## Step 2: Flooring ($30–40)

Interlocking WPC or bamboo tiles (IKEA Runnen, ~$30 for a 9-piece set = ~1 m²). Just click them over your old surface, no glue. The difference is brutal — warm feet instead of cold concrete.

## Step 3: Seating ($40–60)

Folding chairs don’t work — they never unfold, you never sit. Buy **one** comfortable option:
- Rattan armchair with cushion (secondhand, ~$30)
- Fold-out 2-person sofa (JYSK, ~$60)
- Waterproof bean bag (~$40)

Better one quality piece than three uncomfortable ones.

## Step 4: Plants ($20–30)

3–5 plants do more than 20. Basics:
- **Lavender** — blooms, smells, repels mosquitoes
- **Primrose or geraniums** — colorful cascade over the edge
- **Herbs** (basil, mint) — you’ll use them in the kitchen

Buy at hardware store, not florist (half the price).

## Step 5: Lights ($20)

Solar-charged LED string lights from Amazon or IKEA. No cables to run. Turns on at dusk. Instant evening atmosphere.

## Bonus: AI preview

Before you start buying, photograph your balcony and upload to [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) — AI generates 5 styles (Scandinavian, boho, urban, minimal, Mediterranean). You see what works before spending.
